subject: On-prem platform credit tethering and SLA corridor
messages:
From: Aditi Rao <aditi@cloudline.health>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Cloudline Procurement <procurement@cloudline.health>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP Qs — platform credits, amortization, and SLA corridor

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As we prepare our procurement packet I have a couple of follow-ups from the RFP that need explicit language so our finance team can close this out:

1) Platform credit tethering: Cloudline prefers credits that are fungible against monthly invoice lines rather than one-time rebates. We need to understand how Redwood would allow credits to be applied over a 12–24 month amortization window, and whether credits can be scoped to specific nodes/regions (we want credits to apply only to our US on-prem clusters).

2) SLA corridor & credit cliffs: Our SREs expect a clearly defined SLA corridor (e.g., target latency bands + credit percentages per missed band). Can you provide the exact formula Redwood uses to calculate monthly service credits tied to latency and availability shortfalls?

3) Support tier swap: If we upgrade to 24/7 SRE retainer mid-contract, how are prior credits reconciled? Does switching tiers prorate platform credits or is there an offset?

Attaching the RFP and a sample invoice for context.

Can we get a proposal that spells out: amortization period, credit scoping by region/node, SLA credit formula, and an example month where credits are applied?

Best,
Aditi

Attachments: Cloudline_RFP.pdf

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Aditi Rao <aditi@cloudline.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP Qs — platform credits, amortization, and SLA corridor

Hi Aditi — thanks for the clear asks and the RFP. I'll outline a proposal below and follow up with a worksheet we use to model amortization and scoping. High level answers first, then a worked example attached.

- Platform credit tethering: We can offer platform credits that are applied to monthly invoices. Standard practice is a 12-month amortization by default; customers can elect 24 months for larger one-time credits. Credits can be scoped to "site tags" (e.g., us-west-onprem) so they only offset charges for that scope.

- SLA corridor & credit cliffs: We define a two-band SLA for availability and a three-band latency corridor. Credits are applied as a % of platform fee (not core metered usage) per band. Formula example in worksheet: Credit = PlatformFee * BandPenalty% * (DaysNotMet / DaysInMonth).

- Support tier swap: Upgrades are prorated. Unused amortized credit is reallocated to the new monthly schedule; we do not claw back credits already consumed. I'll loop in Marissa (pricing) and Rishi (legal) to harden the wording.

I'm attaching the RIC_Platform_Credit_Worksheet.xlsx with the example you requested. If that looks good we'll convert to contract language.

— Priya
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Please see attached worksheet; need two things:
1) Marissa: propose a credit schedule (both 12mo and 24mo amortization) that preserves platform economics. Include an example month showing invoice before/after credits.
2) Rishi: draft a concise clause for the SOW that defines the SLA corridor, the calculation formula (we prefer PlatformFee * BandPenalty% * (DaysNotMet/DaysInMonth)), and upgrade/proration language for support tier changes.

Thanks,
Priya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP Qs — platform credits, amortization, and SLA corridor

Priya — attaching my redline of the credit schedule and a short example. High level:

- 12-month amortization: default. For credits > $200k we recommend 24-month option but cap at 30% of monthly platform fee per month to avoid negative billing.
- Region scoping: credits can be restricted to a site tag; we'll need Cloudline to declare the tag names in SOW.
- SLA corridor: propose three latency bands (Target, Degraded, Critical) with 0%, 10%, 30% of platform fee credit respectively for the month. Availability shortfalls follow existing % table but applied to platform fee only.
- Support swap: upgrades prorate remaining amortized credits across remaining months; downgrades are not permitted mid-term without reconciliation.

Example month (numbers in worksheet): Invoice pre-credit $120,000 (platform fee $40,000). Monthly credit applied (degraded latency band hit 4 days/30) = $40,000 * 10% * (4/30) = $533.33. Net invoice = $119,466.67.

I've kept language tight so Rishi can drop into the SOW.

- Marissa
Director, Pricing

Attachments: RIC_Platform_Credit_Worksheet.xlsx

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 16:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed language & worked example (Cloudline RFP)

Hi Aditi — thanks for the patience while we pulled this together. Please find a short summary and the proposed contract-ready bullet points below; full worksheet and SOW text are in the linked Drive.

Summary items:
- Amortization: Default 12 months. For credits > $200k Cloudline may elect 24 months. Credits are applied to monthly invoice line items scoped by site tag (we will require the site tag list in the SOW).
- Credit scope: Credits restricted to US on-prem site tags provided at contract signature; credits will not offset hosted API charges outside scope.
- SLA corridor & calculation:
  * Latency bands: Target (no credit), Degraded (10% of monthly platform fee pro-rated by days missed), Critical (30% of monthly platform fee pro-rated).
  * Availability: follow % table in SOW applied to platform fee.
  * Formula: Credit = PlatformFee * BandPenalty% * (DaysNotMet / DaysInMonth).
- Support tier changes: Upgrades to a higher support tier are prorated; remaining amortized credit will be reallocated across the remaining months under the new schedule. Downgrades mid-term require reconciliation (no automatic re-crediting).

Next steps:
1) Review the Drive link and RIC worksheet for the worked example.
2) Confirm whether Cloudline prefers 12 or 24-month amortization.
3) If agreed, we'll produce a short SOW addendum with the explicit clause and an invoice example for signature.

If you want, we can set a 30-minute call Monday 8/31 to walk the finance team through the worksheet.

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
